about: Sign-in methods for protocol v2 (docs/ACCOUNTS.md › Sign-in methods, › Sign-in routes, › Rate limits). Owner: the
Worker builder. Runners: cloud/test/sign_in.test.ts (the Worker, through handle(request, env, now)) and
crates/kanso-sync/tests/conformance.rs (MemoryServer). The step language is auth.json's, which this file extends:
start, values, $name values and captures, patterns, settings/admin/request/raw steps, t, as, path, status,
response, response_headers, capture, note and runner: "worker" all mean what they mean there.
env: the Worker vars each case starts with (strings, as wrangler sets them). A case's env merges over it; a null
value unsets the var. Apple and Google are never configured here.
authenticators: {name: {seed, credential_id}}, each 32 bytes of base64url. The credential is an Ed25519 key whose
RFC 8032 private key is the seed (COSE alg -8), with that credential ID. $cred_<name> is its ID.
WebAuthn in a body: any object holding a "$register" or "$assert" key ({authenticator, challenge, sign_count?,
flags?, origin?, rp_id?}, values resolved first) is replaced by the fields below merged with its other keys.
client_data_json: exactly {"type":"webauthn.create"|"webauthn.get","challenge":<challenge>,"origin":<origin>,
"crossOrigin":false}, in that order, no spaces. origin defaults to https://sync.kansoapp.app, rp_id to
sync.kansoapp.app.
$register gives {credential_id, attestation_object, client_data_json}. attestation_object is the CBOR map
{"fmt":"none","attStmt":{},"authData":bytes}, keys in that order. authData is SHA-256(rp_id) || flags
(default 0x45: UP, UV, AT) || u32be sign_count (default 0) || aaguid (16 bytes of 0x07) || u16be ID length ||
credential ID || the COSE key {1:1, 3:-8, -1:6, -2:<32-byte public key>}, keys in that order. CBOR uses the
shortest heads.
$assert gives {credential_id, authenticator_data, client_data_json, signature}. authenticator_data is
SHA-256(rp_id) || flags (default 0x05: UP, UV) || u32be sign_count (default 1). signature is Ed25519 over
authenticator_data || SHA-256(client_data_json).
github: what the fake GitHub answers. device/code gives {device_code, user_code, verification_uri:
"https://github.com/login/device", expires_in: 900, interval}. The token endpoint pops the case's queue: an empty
queue is authorization_pending; "authorized" is an access token, after which /user gives {id}; "denied" is
access_denied; "slow_down" is slow_down. A step {github: answer} pushes one answer.
A step {repeat: n, steps: [...]} runs its steps n times in order (captures are overwritten). It's for rate limits.
New request routes: passkey_start, passkey_finish, passkey_signup_start, passkey_signup_finish, github_start,
github_poll, social_signup, sign_in_methods (GET /v2/account/sign-in), proof_start, set_password
(POST /v2/account/sign-in/password), passkey_register_start, passkey_register_finish, passkey_remove
(path {credential_id}), identity_start and identity_unlink (path {provider}), and aasa
(GET /.well-known/apple-app-site-association; its body is matched as JSON). The approval_* routes are auth.json's.
Not covered here, because they need Apple or Google: the Apple callback page, nonce_reused, provider_unavailable.
providers.test.ts covers them on the Worker.
proof-account and password-account count per account and device; proof-total (60 an hour) and password-total
(15 per 15 minutes) count per account, after the device's own rule passes.
Expected values follow the spec, except its listed divergences (ACCOUNTS.md › Changes since review). A used,
unknown or expired flow is 400 flow_expired; no proof, or a kind the change doesn't take, is 401 reauth_required.
